headline: H.R. 3755 would have barred government restrictions on abortion services, but the Senate did not take it up, so it never became law.
what_it_does: If adopted, this bill would have prohibited governments from placing many limits on abortion services, including limits on certain drugs, telemedicine, and timing when a delay could risk a patient's health. It would also have barred rules requiring unnecessary medical procedures, medically inaccurate information, or extra in-person visits, and limits before or after fetal viability when a provider finds the pregnancy risks the patient's life or health. Anyone could have sued to enforce it, including the Department of Justice, patients, or providers, and it would have applied to restrictions passed before or after enactment.

who_it_affects.how: They would have been protected from certain government rules on how, where, and when they could offer abortion services.
They would have had easier access to telemedicine, certain drugs, and abortion care without some required visits or disclosures.
They would have been barred from enforcing many existing and future abortion restrictions and could have been sued for violations.
